title: Squatters out within 48 hours
detail: Fast court procedures to clear illegally occupied homes (*okupació*) within 48 hours at most, with public help for vulnerable people; an organic law letting police evict at once if the occupation is caught as it happens.
c: Matches PP; LO 1/2025 already sped up cases. 48 hours depends on court workload, and a home cannot be entered without a court order (art. 18.2 of the Constitution).
pos: Owners are protected from unlawful occupation, which builds confidence in letting homes.
neg: Risk of evicting vulnerable people without proper checks; courts are overloaded, so 48 hours is hard to guarantee.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 1/2025 on the efficiency of the justice system (BOE)

title: Tax relief: rent, mortgage, home-savings account, 5% VAT
detail: Bring back a 15% income tax deduction for rent on a main home, 15% for mortgage payments on a main home, and the home-savings account (*cuenta vivienda*); cut VAT on new main homes from 10% to 5% (with limits on size, price and income), and 5% on social housing. The state would compensate the Generalitat for lost revenue.
c: The 15% mortgage and rent deductions were abolished in 2013 and 2015; in our estimate they fed price rises. The EU directive probably allows 5% VAT on new homes as social policy, but the revenue loss is large.
pos: Lower costs for tenants and buyers.
neg: In our estimate the mortgage deduction (abolished in 2013) fed price rises; costly for the Treasury.

s.t: Ley 16/2012: end of the home-purchase deduction (BOE)
Ley 26/2014: end of the rent deduction in income tax from 2015 (BOE)
Directive (EU) 2022/542 on VAT rates (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Ban funds and banks from buying homes until 2028
detail: Until 2028, ban financial institutions and their property arms, investment funds and asset managers from buying homes.
c: Banning banks and funds from buying homes breaches EU free movement of capital and freedom of enterprise (art. 38 of the Constitution). Banks also have to take homes in mortgage enforcement.

title: Boost rental supply with tax breaks, not price caps
detail: Wider insurance against unpaid rent, tax incentives for landlords who let at affordable prices, lower taxes on building and renovating affordable homes, and *SOCIMI* tax breaks only for real affordable build-to-rent. The programme openly criticises rent caps (*topalls de preus*), saying they "do not create new flats".
c: The tax incentives are realistic; "no price caps" directly contradicts PSOE, Sumar and ERC policy, the main point of friction in any possible coalition.
pos: Incentives draw investors in and increase rental supply.
neg: Without price caps, tenants in stressed cities lose protection.

title: Self-determination and independence
detail: Guarantee Catalonia's right to self-determination "by all necessary democratic means"; any referendum agreed with the state should offer the same choice as on 1 October 2017; the path to a "free Catalonia" is described as non-violent "democratic confrontation".
c: As with ERC: self-determination is impossible without constitutional reform under art. 168. "All necessary means" raises questions after the events of 2017.

title: Catalan language as a condition for *arraigo*; ban face veils
detail: Require knowledge of Catalan for *arraigo* (residence based on settled ties) and for permit renewals; ban clothing that fully or largely covers the face in public places (niqab, burqa; the hijab is not affected), under a bill Junts tabled in February 2026.
c: Language requirements for *arraigo* are a state power; requiring Catalan rather than Spanish conflicts with a single nationwide immigration regime.

title: A Catalan economic agreement outside the common system
detail: A law for a Catalan economic agreement (*concert econòmic*) outside the common regional funding law (*LOFCA*), with the Catalan Tax Agency collecting and inspecting all taxes raised in Catalonia, as in the Basque Country, and 100% of the Generalitat's *FLA* debt written off.
c: As with ERC: a *concierto* outside LOFCA exists in the Constitution only for the historic territories. In our estimate, based on INE data, Catalonia produces about 19% of Spain's GDP: taking it out of the common system would hit the other regions hard.

title: Index income tax to inflation; scrap inheritance tax
detail: Index income tax (*IRPF*) to inflation every year, cut the lowest bands and raise personal and family allowances; abolish inheritance and gift tax (*Impuesto de Sucesiones*); lower VAT on hairdressers (21% to 10%) and on care homes and home care.
c: Indexing income tax is the same idea as PP's. Inheritance tax is regional; abolishing it at state level would need a new funding model, but Catalonia can zero it out itself.
pos: A lower tax burden on the middle class.
neg: Lost revenue; cutting inheritance tax benefits the wealthy most.
